name: connect_telemetry
title: Connect to telemetry (Prometheus or Datadog, Jaeger/Tempo, bill)
description: Point Hindcast at the system's live telemetry and probe it, read-only: which metric presets Prometheus (or Datadog) supports, which services it names, how far back data goes, what is missing; which services Jaeger or Tempo knows and which ones requests enter through. Traces are optional: without them, who calls whom is read from service-mesh (Istio, Linkerd), service-graph or span metrics, Datadog's APM service dependencies, or a topologyFile, and the model says what that loses. Saves the connection in the workspace (credentials only as env var names). Call this first; calling it again merges new settings. Returns problems to fix and what the model will be able to know.

selector.description: label matchers added to every query, e.g. cluster="prod-eu"

namespaces.description: Kubernetes namespaces the system runs in (default: the namespaces holding the traced services)

calls.description: without traces: which metrics name who calls whom, where several do (default: the first found of istio, linkerd, servicegraph, spanmetrics)

presets.description: default: every preset whose metrics exist

tokenEnv.description: env var holding a bearer token (the token itself never goes in the workspace)

datadog.description: Datadog instead of Prometheus, read-only through its Metrics API: APM trace metrics, the Agent's Kubernetes metrics and ingress-nginx; who calls whom from APM service dependencies. Keys only as env var names

site.description: your Datadog site: datadoghq.com, us3.datadoghq.com, us5.datadoghq.com, datadoghq.eu, ap1.datadoghq.com, ap2.datadoghq.com, ddog-gov.com

url.description: the API base instead of a site (a proxy), e.g. https://api.datadoghq.com

apiKeyEnv.description: env var holding the API key (default DD_API_KEY); the key itself is never accepted or written

appKeyEnv.description: env var holding the application key (default DD_APP_KEY); it needs metrics_read, timeseries_query and apm_read

env.description: the APM env to read (default: the busiest env in the trace metrics)

scope.description: a tag filter added to every query, e.g. kube_cluster_name:prod-eu

namespaces.description: Kubernetes namespaces the system runs in (default: the namespaces holding the APM services)

presets.description: default: every preset whose metrics exist

url.description: Jaeger query UI/API base, e.g. http://jaeger:16686

tokenEnv.description: env var holding a bearer token (the token itself never goes in the workspace)

url.description: Tempo HTTP API base, e.g. http://tempo:3200

tokenEnv.description: env var holding a bearer token (the token itself never goes in the workspace)

traceFiles.description: OTLP JSON lines or Jaeger JSON files (globs ok), instead of a trace backend

topologyFile.description: without traces: a YAML file of who calls whom — calls: { caller: [callees] } or { caller: { callee: callsPerRequest } }, optional entry: [services] and grpc: [services]. Without traces or this file, calls are read from mesh, service-graph or span metrics

cur.description: AWS Cost and Usage Report CSV

tag.description: cost-allocation tag naming the component, e.g. user:service

timeoutMs.description: client deadline: slower answers count as failures

rename.description: raw service names → one id across sources

hostedBy.description: in-process dependencies seen in traces → the service they run in

entry.description: services requests enter through (default: found in traces)

ignore.description: services outside the system, e.g. load generators (default: client-only services in traces)

exclude.description: services to drop from the collected history: another system sharing the Prometheus (collect_telemetry lists services no trace touches)

include.description: workloads to keep that would be left out as observability tooling (jaeger, otel-collector, prometheus, grafana, *-exporter…), when they are part of the system being modelled

placement.description: service → where it runs, for data-transfer pricing: { checkout: { zone: "us-east-1a", region: "us-east-1" } }

name: collect_telemetry
title: Collect history from the connected telemetry
description: Query Prometheus (or Datadog) over a window, fetch traces spread across it from Jaeger/Tempo (without them, read who calls whom from the metrics), add the bill, and import everything into the workspace dataset. Reports per service which signals exist (request rate, errors, p99, CPU, CPU limit, replicas, traces) and what is missing. Longer history with a busy peak makes a better model: one overload in the history is worth more than a month of quiet days.

last.description: how much history, e.g. "6h", "7d", "14d" (default 24h, or what the data covers)

start.description: window start (ISO or epoch s), instead of last

end.description: window end (default now, or the newest data)

stepS.description: bucket size in seconds (default: window / ~1000, at least 30)

maxTraces.description: traces to fetch, spread over the window (default 3000)

windows.description: several windows instead of one — an ordinary week plus a load test, say. A calm history never shows where latency turns; one load test in it teaches the model

name: calibrate_model
title: Calibrate a model of the system from the collected history
description: Fit the model: capacity per replica (with its band) and what limits it (CPU, a lock or pool), latency, errors and cost per service; endpoint paths from traces. Holds back the last part of the history to measure accuracy on data the model never saw. Returns a trust report: services whose limit the history actually reached, services whose capacity is extrapolated, and services the model cannot explain. Read it before relying on verify_change.

holdout.description: share of the history held back to measure accuracy (default 0.3; 0 to skip)

listPrices.description: price services without a bill line at AWS Fargate list prices (default true)

name: model_status
title: What the workspace holds
description: Connections, the collected history (window, age), the model (fit and trust per service, accuracy), recent reports, warnings (stale history, unmeasured accuracy) and the next step. Cheap: call it at the start of a session to see what is already there.

name: verify_change
title: Verify an infrastructure change against real history
description: Backtest one or more changes over the collected history, before they ship: $ per month saved or spent (with its 10–90% band), minutes out of SLO added or removed, failed requests, the worst moment and why, endpoints that get worse, headroom before and after. A change is a strategy (object or YAML), a Kubernetes manifest diff (base/head), a Terraform plan (`terraform show -json`), or edited manifests against the live cluster snapshot from read_cluster. Each result has verdict pass | fail | inconclusive and a confidence (high | medium | low) that says which services the change pushes past anything the history showed. With a baseline (an approved change not yet deployed, e.g. the pull request this one is stacked on), the baseline is applied to both sides, already running, and every verdict, delta and gate is about the change on top of it. Writes an HTML and Markdown report for a human. A low-confidence result that asks for a load test: plan_load_test with the same changes designs it.

strategy.description: a strategy object or YAML: { name, changes: [{ service, replicas | autoscale | cpu | memoryGb | cpuRequest | memoryRequestGb | arch | perf | capacityRps | cache | readReplicas | zone | region | runtime } | { endpoint, retries, timeoutMs }] }

base.description: manifests before: a directory, a file, or YAML text

terraformPlan.description: path to `terraform show -json plan.out` output, or the JSON itself

head.description: the edited manifests (directory, file or YAML text)

baseline.description: a change already approved but not yet deployed, in any shape a change takes: applied to the as-built side and to every change's side, its pods running before the window, so each change is judged on what it adds on top of it ("assuming PR #1 goes in, is PR #2 safe?"). For a Kubernetes baseline give the change's base as the baseline's head, or as what runs: settings the change makes the same as the baseline are left to the baseline

strategy.description: a strategy object or YAML: { name, changes: [{ service, replicas | autoscale | cpu | memoryGb | cpuRequest | memoryRequestGb | arch | perf | capacityRps | cache | readReplicas | zone | region | runtime } | { endpoint, retries, timeoutMs }] }

base.description: manifests before: a directory, a file, or YAML text

terraformPlan.description: path to `terraform show -json plan.out` output, or the JSON itself

head.description: the edited manifests (directory, file or YAML text)

last.description: only the last part of the history, e.g. "7d"

gateMinutes.description: minutes out of SLO a change may add before it fails (default 0.5)

window.description: replay only this part of the history — the ordinary week, when the history also holds a load test (the model still learned from all of it)

traffic.description: replay the history at another load — scale ×N, or peakRps for its busiest moment — to ask "does it survive launch day / Black Friday?"; the as-built system sees the same load

report.description: false: write no report files (the HTML, Markdown and app bundle under reports/ in the workspace); default true

name: suggest_changes
title: What should we change? Fixes and savings, backtested
description: Generates candidate changes from the history itself and backtests them all: services that ran out of capacity get fixes (more replicas — of the host for an in-process dependency —, more CPU or CPU autoscaling when CPU-bound); services that idled get savings (fewer replicas, smaller CPU, Graviton). Returns the fixes that cut minutes out of SLO and the savings that pass, cheapest first, each with its verdict and confidence, the passing savings tried together, and what was rejected. Use it for "what should we change?", "where can we save?" or after a fail, then verify_change the one to ship.

idleBelow.description: a service is idle below this share of capacity at its busiest (default 0.35)

traffic.description: replay the history at another load — scale ×N, or peakRps for its busiest moment — and suggest what that day needs ("what do we change before launch day?"); every candidate is judged at that load

name: find_headroom
title: How much more traffic the system can take
description: The req/s the calibrated model sustains within SLO with today's endpoint mix, and which service saturates first — as built, and optionally with a strategy applied.

name: review_capacity
title: Capacity review: headroom, busier days, node loss, binding limits, fixes and savings
description: The capacity review a platform team does by hand, from the calibrated history, every number backtested: headroom over the busiest moment and what saturates first; whether 1.5× and 2× today's traffic hold; what losing a node at the peak costs and the single points of failure (Kubernetes), with the replicas that fix it; services held back by CPU quota throttling or near their memory limit; and the fixes and savings that pass. Writes a Markdown report into the workspace that opens with a five-line summary (risk, headroom, cost, the one change to make, how far to trust it) — lead your answer with it. Use it for "how are we doing?", "weekly capacity review", "are we ready for next week?".

name: plan_load_test
title: Plan the load test an inconclusive verdict asks for (k6 script and follow-up)
description: The load test an inconclusive verdict asks for. When verify_change says a change would run a service at a share of capacity the history never tested ("load-test before trusting it"), this says which services need evidence and up to what request rate (the rate the change needs, with margin), at which entry endpoints in the recorded mix (who calls whom decides what reaches each service), writes a step-load k6 script into the workspace (from the history's peak to the target, each step held a calibration bucket or more, aborting per step at the SLO's error rate and p99; base URL and auth from env var names, never credentials), says where to run it and what it costs, and gives the exact follow-up: collect_telemetry with the test's window beside the history, calibrate_model, verify_change again, and what the answer is expected to change. Takes the same changes as verify_change, or a list of services. Runs nothing against the system.

strategy.description: a strategy object or YAML: { name, changes: [{ service, replicas | autoscale | cpu | memoryGb | cpuRequest | memoryRequestGb | arch | perf | capacityRps | cache | readReplicas | zone | region | runtime } | { endpoint, retries, timeoutMs }] }

base.description: manifests before: a directory, a file, or YAML text

terraformPlan.description: path to `terraform show -json plan.out` output, or the JSON itself

head.description: the edited manifests (directory, file or YAML text)

changes.description: the changes, as verify_change takes them: the plan drives every service a change runs past what the history showed

services.description: services to drive directly, without a change: each to `utilization` of its modelled capacity (default 0.9)

traffic.description: replay the history at another load — scale ×N, or peakRps for its busiest moment — to ask "does it survive launch day / Black Friday?"; the as-built system sees the same load

last.description: only the last part of the history, e.g. "7d"

window.description: replay only this part of the history, as verify_change does: the plan's follow-up keeps it

gateMinutes.description: minutes out of SLO a change may add before it fails (default 0.5)

draws.description: capacity draws for the replay the targets are read from (default 8)

margin.description: how far past what the change needs to drive each service (default 1.1); a service is never driven past 90% of its capacity unless asked

steps.description: load steps from the history's peak to the target (default 5)

holdS.description: seconds each step is held (default two calibration buckets, at least 120), rounded up to whole buckets

mix.description: focused (default): only the entry endpoints that reach the services to test, in their recorded proportions; recorded: every endpoint

replicas.description: replicas per service where the test runs, when they differ from the model's (e.g. a smaller staging)

baseUrlEnv.description: env var the script reads the base URL from (default BASE_URL)

authEnv.description: env var whose value the script sends as the Authorization header when set (default AUTH_HEADER); never the credential itself

name: check_node_loss
title: Does it survive losing a Kubernetes node at its busiest?
description: Replays the history's busiest moment with each node gone: every pod on it disappears at once (from kube_pod_info placement at the end of the history), services left with no replica are down, the rest serve on what is left, and Kubernetes brings the pods back after NotReady plus the default 300 s eviction toleration and a start (or never, when a fixed node pool has no room). Returns per node what it takes down, the minutes out of SLO and failed requests it adds, and the services one node failure takes out entirely. With a strategy, its replica changes are spread evenly over the nodes. Use it for "can we lose a node?", "is 2 replicas enough?", "where are our single points of failure?".

strategy.description: check under this strategy instead of as built

zones.description: lose a whole availability zone (every node in it) instead of one node — zones come from the nodes' provider ids (AWS, GCP)

name: verify_design
title: Verify a system design (no history needed)
description: Check an architecture spec an agent wrote or proposes: validate it, simulate it at the expected load, replay every failure (instance and component deaths, zone loss, slow and erroring dependencies, cold caches, a 3× surge), measure headroom and cost against a budget. Verdict pass | pass with risks | fail, with findings and verified fixes that list the exact spec changes to apply. Use list_components to write the spec. Numbers come from catalogue defaults unless the spec overrides capacity, latency and cost.

rps.description: expected load (default: half the breaking point)

budgetMonthly.description: $ per month the design must fit in

incidentCostPerMinute.description: what a minute of outage costs, to price risk

name: read_cluster
title: Snapshot a Kubernetes cluster's workloads (read-only)
description: Run `kubectl get deployments,statefulsets,hpa -o json` against an explicitly named context and save the snapshot: replicas, CPU and memory limits, autoscalers and architecture per workload. Never uses the current context implicitly and never runs anything but get. Then verify_change with { cluster: { head } } backtests edited manifests against what is running.

context.description: kube context name — required, never implied
